purpose: Human sense selection and child-definition authoring. Candidate glosses are reference-only CC-BY material and are never copied automatically into runtime knowledge.

sourceSense.definition: of a very early stage in development
examples: Old English is also called Anglo Saxon
Old High German is High German from the middle of the 9th to the end of the 11th century

sourceSense.definition: (used especially of persons) having lived for a relatively long time or attained a specific age
of long duration; not new
containing as much or as many as is possible or normal
examples: the auditorium was full to overflowing

sourceSense.definition: constituting the full quantity or extent; complete
examples: an entire town devastated by an earthquake

sourceSense.definition: complete in extent or degree and in every particular
acting or moving or capable of acting or moving quickly
examples: on the fast track in school

sourceSense.definition: (used of timepieces) indicating a time ahead of or later than the correct time
at a rapid tempo
examples: the band played a fast fox trot

sourceSense.definition: change location; move, travel, or proceed, also metaphorically
examples: How fast does your new car go?
We travelled from Rome to Naples by bus
The policemen went from door to door looking for the suspect
The soldiers moved towards the city in an attempt to take it before night fell

sourceSense.definition: follow a procedure or take a course
examples: We should go farther in this matter
She went through a lot of trouble
go about the world in a certain manner
Messages must go through diplomatic channels

sourceSense.definition: move away from a place into another direction
examples: Go away before I start to cry

sourceSense.definition: move toward, travel toward something or somebody or approach something or somebody
examples: He came singing down the road
Come with me to the Casbah

sourceSense.definition: reach a destination; arrive by movement or progress
examples: She didn't get to Chicago until after midnight

sourceSense.definition: come to pass; arrive, as in due course
examples: The first success came three days later

sourceSense.definition: come upon, as if by accident; meet with
examples: We find this idea in Plato
I happened upon the most wonderful bakery not very far from here
She chanced upon an interesting book in the bookstore the other day

sourceSense.definition: discover or determine the existence, presence, or fact of by perception with the eyes
examples: She detected high levels of lead in her drinking water
We found traces of lead in the paint

sourceSense.definition: come upon after searching; find the location of something that was missed or lost
put into a certain place or abstract location
examples: Set the dogs on the scent of the missing children
Place emphasis on a certain point

sourceSense.definition: cause to be in a certain state; cause to be in a certain relation
examples: That song put me in awful good humor

sourceSense.definition: formulate in a particular style or language
examples: I wouldn't put it that way
She cast her request in very polite language

sourceSense.definition: relatively large in size or number or extent; larger than others of its kind
of major significance or importance
examples: Einstein was one of the outstanding figures of the 20th century

sourceSense.definition: remarkable or out of the ordinary in degree or magnitude or effect
examples: had a great stake in the outcome

sourceSense.definition: make a request or demand for something to somebody
examples: She asked him for a loan

sourceSense.definition: direct or put; seek an answer to
consider obligatory; request and expect
examples: We require our secretary to be on time
Aren't we asking too much of these children?
I expect my students to arrive in time for their lessons

sourceSense.definition: a strong positive emotion of regard and affection
examples: children need a lot of love

sourceSense.definition: any object of warm affection or devotion
examples: the theater was her first love
he has a passion for cock fighting

sourceSense.definition: a beloved person; used as terms of endearment
a dwelling that serves as living quarters for one or more families
examples: he has a house on Cape Cod
she felt she had to get out of the house

sourceSense.definition: the members of a business organization that owns or operates one or more establishments
examples: he worked for a brokerage house

sourceSense.definition: the members of a religious community living together
an educational institution
a building where young people receive education
examples: he walked to school every morning

sourceSense.definition: the process of being formally educated at a school
examples: what will you do when you finish school?

sourceSense.definition: unlike in nature or quality or form or degree
examples: took different approaches to the problem
on different sides of the issue
this meeting was different from the earlier one

sourceSense.definition: distinctly separate from the first
differing from all others; not ordinary
examples: advertising that strives continually to be different
this new music is certainly different but I don't really like it

sourceSense.definition: the organization that is the governing authority of a political unit
examples: the matter was referred to higher authorities

sourceSense.definition: the act of governing; exercising authority
examples: regulations for the governing of state prisons
he had considerable experience of government

sourceSense.definition: (government) the system or form by which a community or other political unit is governed
any number of entities (members) considered as a unit
(chemistry) two or more atoms bound together as a single unit and forming part of a molecule
a set that is closed, associative, has an identity element and every element has an inverse

binary compound that occurs at room temperature as a clear colorless odorless tasteless liquid; freezes into ice below 0 degrees centigrade and boils above 100 degrees centigrade; widely used as a solvent
the part of the earth's surface covered with water (such as a river or lake or ocean)
examples: they were sitting by the water's edge

sourceSense.definition: once thought to be one of four elements composing the universe (Empedocles), associated with the humour phlegm
a category of things distinguished by some common characteristic or quality
examples: sculpture is a form of art
what kinds of desserts are there?

sourceSense.definition: of great significance or value
examples: the important questions of the day

sourceSense.definition: important in effect or meaning
examples: a significant change in tax laws
a significant change in the Constitution

sourceSense.definition: of extreme importance; vital to the resolution of a crisis
examples: a crucial moment in his career

sourceSense.definition: at or near the beginning of a period of time or course of events or before the usual or expected time
examples: early varieties of peas and tomatoes mature before most standard varieties

sourceSense.definition: being or occurring at an early stage of development
belonging to the distant past
the aggregate of past events
examples: a critical time in the school's history

sourceSense.definition: a record or narrative description of past events
examples: he gave an inaccurate account of the plot to kill the president
the story of exposure to lead

sourceSense.definition: the discipline that records and interprets past events involving human beings
a member of the Religious Society of Friends founded by George Fox (the Friends have never called themselves Quakers)
a person you know well and regard with affection and trust
examples: he was my best friend at the university

sourceSense.definition: an associate who provides cooperation or assistance
examples: he's a good ally in fight

sourceSense.definition: a collection of things sharing a common attribute
examples: there are two classes of detergents

sourceSense.definition: a body of students who are taught together
examples: early morning classes are always sleepy

sourceSense.definition: people having the same social, economic, or educational status
the time that has elapsed
a earlier period in someone's life (especially one that they have reason to keep secret)
examples: reporters dug into the candidate's past

sourceSense.definition: a verb tense that expresses actions or states in the past
capable of happening or existing
examples: a breakthrough may be possible next year

sourceSense.definition: existing in possibility
a small portable timepiece
a period of time (4 or 2 hours) during which some of a ship's crew are on duty
a purposeful surveillance to guard or observe
a young person of either sex
examples: ‘tiddler’ is a British term for youngster

sourceSense.definition: a human offspring (son or daughter) of any age
examples: they were able to send their kids to college

sourceSense.definition: an immature childish person
examples: he remained a child in practical matters as long as he lived

sourceSense.definition: the accumulation of knowledge or skill that results from direct participation in events or activities
the content of direct observation or participation in an event
an event as apprehended
examples: that painful experience certainly got our attention

sourceSense.definition: anew
in accordance with nature; relating to or concerning nature
existing in or produced by nature; not artificial or imitation
existing in or in conformity with nature or the observable world; neither supernatural nor magical
a systematic means of communicating by the use of sounds or conventional symbols
examples: the language introduced is standard throughout the text
the speed with which a program can be executed depends on the language in which it is written

sourceSense.definition: (language) communication by word of mouth
examples: he recorded the spoken language of the streets

sourceSense.definition: the text of a popular song or musical-comedy number
examples: his compositions always started with the lyrics
he wrote both words and music

sourceSense.definition: regarded with great favor, approval, or affection especially by the general public
examples: cabbage patch dolls are no longer popular

sourceSense.definition: carried on by or for the people (or citizens) at large
representing or appealing to or adapted for the benefit of the people at large
in these times
examples: it is solely by their language that the upper classes nowadays are distinguished
we now rarely see horse-drawn vehicles on city streets
today almost every home has television

sourceSense.definition: on this day as distinct from yesterday or tomorrow
examples: I can't meet with you today

sourceSense.definition: on one occasion
as soon as
examples: once we are home, we can rest

sourceSense.definition: at a previous time
examples: at one time he loved her

sourceSense.definition: having a low or inadequate temperature or feeling a sensation of coldness or having been made cold by e.g. ice or refrigeration
examples: if you are cold, turn up the heat

sourceSense.definition: extended meanings; especially of psychological coldness; without human warmth or emotion
having lost freshness through passage of time
examples: dogs attempting to catch a cold scent

sourceSense.definition: a land mass (smaller than a continent) that is surrounded by water
a zone or area resembling an island
recall knowledge from memory; have a recollection
examples: I can't remember saying any such thing
I can't think what her last name was
can you remember her phone number?
Do you remember that he once loved you?

sourceSense.definition: keep in mind for attention or consideration
examples: Remember to call your mother every day!
Think of the starving children in India!

sourceSense.definition: recapture the past; indulge in memories
examples: he remembered how he used to pick flowers

sourceSense.definition: cause to continue in a certain state, position, or activity
examples: She always held herself as a lady
The students keep me on my toes

sourceSense.definition: have or hold in one's hands or grip
examples: Hold this bowl for a moment, please

sourceSense.definition: organize or be responsible for
examples: have, throw, or make a party

sourceSense.definition: gain knowledge or skills
examples: She learned dancing from her sister
Children acquire language at an amazing rate

sourceSense.definition: get to know or become aware of, usually accidentally
examples: I learned that she has two grown-up children
I see that you have been promoted

sourceSense.definition: commit to memory; learn by heart
examples: Have you memorized your lines for the play yet?

sourceSense.definition: an adult female person (as opposed to a man)
examples: the woman kept house while the man hunted

sourceSense.definition: a female person who plays a significant role (wife or mistress or girlfriend) in the life of a particular man
examples: he was faithful to his woman

sourceSense.definition: women as a class
examples: it's an insult to American womanhood
woman is the glory of creation
the fair sex gathered on the veranda

sourceSense.definition: ‘Father’ is a term of address for priests in some churches (especially the Roman Catholic Church or the Orthodox Catholic Church); ‘Padre’ is frequently used in the military

(Christianity) any of about 70 theologians in the period from the 2nd to the 7th century whose writing established and confirmed official church doctrine; in the Roman Catholic Church some were later declared saints and became Doctor of the Church; the best known Latin Church Fathers are Ambrose, Augustine, Gregory the Great, and Jerome; those who wrote in Greek include Athanasius, Basil, Gregory Nazianzen, and John Chrysostom
a male parent (also used as a term of address to your father)
examples: his father was born in Atlanta
